Beijing, Aug 30: Chinese officials on Sunday said 261 foreign nationals, including 49 Indians, remained unaccounted for after a catastrophic flash flood struck Gyirong Port, one of the main border crossings between Nepal and Tibet, on August 26.
The 261 foreigners are from 23 countries, Chinese officials told a media briefing at Gyirong, state-run Xinhua news agency reported.
The media briefing was held after a joint search and cross-checking of information by foreign affairs, public security, culture and tourism, and emergency management authorities.
Those unaccounted for include 104 people from Nepal, 49 from India, 33 from Latvia, 18 from the United States, 15 from Britain, six from Canada, six from Australia, four from South Africa, three each from Malaysia, Germany and Russia, two each from Ireland, Estonia, France, Netherlands, New Zealand, and one each from Kazakhstan, Finland, Lithuania, Portugal, Ukraine, Spain and Hungary, it reported.
A large number of Indian pilgrims were visiting Tibet to take part in the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra after ties between China and India improved.
Some of the Indian pilgrims were reportedly at the immigration building at the Tibet-Nepal border when the flood struck the region, wreaking havoc in Gyirong County in Tibet.
Videos of the giant flash flood engulfing the sprawling immigration building went viral globally.

Most people know that Labor Day is one of the best times of the year to buy tools (get it? Labor?), but if you’re a newly minted homeowner or DIY-er, the landscape can be intimidating. When I bought my first home, I owned only two screwdrivers, a pair of pliers, and a hammer; I had no clue what I was in for.
Now that I’ve been a homeowner for 17 years, I agree with WIRED reviewer Scott Gilbertson that unless you’re a professional tradesperson or really love large projects, you don’t need a garage full of specialty tools. Just the basics will do: a drill, a saw, a set of manual screwdrivers, and a stud finder, for example.
Luckily, early Labor Day deals are pretty decent this year. In fact, after examining all the major sales, I was able to find a rather encyclopedic house-repair kit for any new homeowner or DIY-er for under $375 (minus tax and shipping) with deals from Home Depot, Lowe’s, and Walmart. Any of these would also be great to stash away for a holiday gift.
Here’s what I chose:
Power-Tool Workhorses: Ryobi 4-Tool Kit for $199
Look, you’re not going to take Ryobi tools to a jobsite or use them to build a house from scratch (a former WIRED editor once deemed them “the Kia of tools”), but if you’re just using them for basic, casual home use, they’ll do the job. Ryobi’s 18V ONE+ batteries (this set comes with one) are fully backward compatible with all Ryobi tools ever made, and this set has a three-year warranty. I live in a DeWalt household, so I don’t have a lot of firsthand experience with Ryobi, but my brother, a contractor, says the brand is great for the average DIY homeowner and offers a much broader range of tools than competitor Bauer from Harbor Freight.
This set packs a ½-inch drill/driver, an impact driver (which WIRED reviewer Scott Gilbertson said had a profound 'I can't believe I didn't own one sooner' impact on him, though his is Milwaukee), a circular saw, and an LED light. The impact driver packs 1,800 pounds of torque, which is pretty decent for a consumer-level tool. If you need a sander, there's also another kit with a sander plus drill/driver and circular saw, which may be worth a look if this set sells out.
The Hand-Tool Essentials: Workpro 408-Piece Set for $144
I don't have this exact set, but I do have remnants of a similar one. Again, you're not going to bring these to a construction site, but this kit is a knockout deal for everything you get—pliers, screwdrivers, Allen keys, wrenches, sockets, bits, tape measure, knife, hammer, wire stripper … there's even a metal box in which to store everything. A lot of the “pieces” are doodads like screwdriver heads and drywall anchors, but it still contains pretty much any non-power tool you might need for light home repairs and even basic car maintenance. (There's no level, but you can always use an app on your phone for that.) However, note that this is a flash deal, so it's likely only live for a limited time.
Wall-Hanging Must-Have: Franklin Sensors Stud Finder for $22
No household repair kit is complete without a stud finder. (And if you're a dad, it will give you years of built-in dad jokes.) In fact, you can't—or, at least, shouldn't—hang anything even slightly heavy on your wall without one. I have a Franklin Sensors stud finder, though not this exact model, and it's done well to help my family hang pictures, shelves, mirrors, and pretty much everything else for the past decade or so. The Terrible Movie That Chinese Audiences Can’t Stop Watching
Viewers are flocking to a new film that captures the pleasure of bad art.
One of the only compliments I can offer the new Chinese animated film Niu Lai is that it certainly qualifies as a film. There is sound. The pictures move. But beyond the basics of what makes a movie a movie, Niu Lai, which translates to “The Ox Comes,” contains little artistic merit. The plot, about a calf coming of age with the help of a leopard, a bird, and his mother, is thin, and the characters have been so nightmarishly rendered on a rudimentary computer program that they might as well be sleep-paralysis demons.
Yet Niu Lai has become a bona fide box-office hit in China. Since a small distributor unceremoniously dumped it in theaters in early August, the film has become one of the most lucrative movies in Chinese history, making more than $7 million off a reported budget of no more than $500 and outperforming recent blockbusters such as The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Much of its success is thanks to Chinese social media, where clips of it first went viral: Some users have embraced Niu Lai as a meme, purchasing tickets so they could ridicule the baffling work with an audience. Others have championed the project as anti-AI art, arguing that it deserves to be appreciated as a purely human creation. As flawed as Niu Lai may be, to the fans, it’s at least better than AI slop.
I’m not so sure about that. Watching a bootleg version of Niu Lai felt painful but apt: What better way was there to see a jankily made film than in potato quality on my computer at home? Instead, what’s distinctly human about Niu Lai comes from everything around it: how it was made, how it became a sensation, and how it has inspired further creativity in turn. Theater workers have drawn posters by hand to help advertise the movie. Businesses have made plush toys of the bovine hero. Fans have donned cow masks for screenings, and although the film isn’t available in the United States, underground viewings have popped up in major cities. As such, Niu Lai is the rare passion project that has attracted audiences not because it’s so bad that it’s good, but because it’s an occasion to celebrate the ability to have an original idea at all.
Never mind that the idea was apparently underdeveloped from the start. The first-time director, Xin Yumeng, explained in an interview that he wanted to write about an ox because that’s his father’s zodiac symbol; the year he began working on it also happened to be 2021, the year of the ox. Production took five years, as the then-29-year-old Xin and his mother, Sun Lifang, wrote the screenplay together and made up the entire crew and cast: Sun sang the theme song, and Xin animated the 86-minute film frame by frame on SketchUp, an architectural-modeling program. The process was grueling, Xin said, adding that he kept going in part because he saw the story as a way to inspire viewers to not tang ping, or “lie flat,” referring to a societal trend in 2021 where young people in China rejected overworking by cheekily glorifying the act of lying down.
In some ways, the movie is a deeply Chinese phenomenon: Fuzzy cartoon characters tend to become popular in the country—Zootopia 2 is the highest-grossing Hollywood film ever released there—and the words niu lai could also refer to the coming of a bull market, which has led some Chinese stock investors to purchase tickets for good luck. Plus, Niu Lai’s threadbare plot is rooted in the principle of filial piety, as the titular protagonist learns to respect and care for his mother.
The Niu Lai phenomenon also seems to embody a phrase that’s gained traction lately in China: huo ren gan, which, translated literally, means “alive-human feeling.” The film expresses this quality, but not only because Xi didn’t use AI to help create it. What makes Niu Lai stand out most is its unabashed sincerity. It is an earnest attempt to tell a fable about a naive cow, and the story of its making is deeply charming: Here is a mother-son duo, total outsiders to the entertainment industry, trying their best to turn their quixotic idea into reality. Making a movie anywhere requires overcoming so many hurdles that have nothing to do with art or creativity; there are budgets to be balanced and business expectations to be met. But Niu Lai is a modest reminder that any film simply begins with an idea and an irrepressible urge to see it through.

A Greenlandic commission is to present a highly anticipated report Friday to determine whether Denmark's forced contraception of thousands of the Arctic island's indigenous Inuit constituted a "genocide".
The forced contraception campaign between the 1960s and 1990 is one of the darkest chapters in Greenland's history with its former colonial master, Denmark.
Once the conclusions are presented, Greenland's government will decide how to move forward.
"For us, it's about trying to understand our history," Naaja Nathanielsen, a member of parliament representing Greenland in Denmark's parliament, told AFP.
"Others may feel that we should simply keep quiet about this and try to be conciliatory, because of the United States' aggressiveness toward Greenland."
Nathanielsen announced the creation of the commission, tasked with shedding light on the legal implications of the campaign, in August 2024 when she was Greenland's minister of justice and gender equality.
During the 1960s to 1990, more than 4,000 Greenlandic women were forced to wear a contraceptive coil -- or intrauterine device (IUD) -- in the vast majority of cases without their consent or that of their parents if they were minors.
Greenland, a Danish colony for three centuries and now an autonomous territory, still has a complicated relationship with Copenhagen.
Despite many thorny issues between them, both Copenhagen and Nuuk have presented a united front rejecting US President Donald Trump's threats to take over Greenland.
He has repeatedly accused Denmark of treating Greenland badly.
"Everything that is happening between Denmark and Greenland now is scrutinised," said historian Astrid Andersen, a researcher at the Danish Institute for International Studies (DIIS).
"There's this pressure on the relationship so of course, when we start talking about genocide, that increases the pressure.
"But everyone in Greenland has been very clear that this tragic case should not be used to legitimise other political purposes internationally."
The commission's four appointed experts were unable to agree on which approach to take and ended up writing two reports, submitted nearly six months behind schedule.
Not just about history
One of the victims, Henriette Berthelsen, told AFP the conclusions, regardless of what is decided, were skewed from the start since no Greenlandic Inuit were appointed as experts.
"For me, this is not just about history or politics. It's my body, my life, and my right to self-determination," she said.
"And once again, I see that it is others who will investigate and define what was done to me and to other Inuit women."
The campaign affected girls as young as 12, some of whom were never able to have children afterwards.
Nuuk and Copenhagen are also shedding light on several other painful chapters from the past, including children adopted without parental consent or torn from their families.
On Thursday, the Danish parliament agreed that women affected by the forced contraception campaign can claim compensation from Copenhagen, an initiative pushed by Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen who presented Denmark's official apology last year.
Beyond imagination
Media coverage of the case has revived trauma that had been buried for decades.
"I realised everything it had cost me -- all those hospitalisations, those surgeries, the schooling I missed and, above all, those pains I had never associated with that damn IUD," said Kirstine Najarak Berthelsen.
"It was buried so deeply in my subconscious... Everything that happened to people is beyond imagination if you haven't experienced it yourself," she added.
By the late 1970s, one in two Greenlandic women of childbearing age -- at least 4,070 women -- had been fitted with an IUD, according to an investigation presented in September 2025.
The scandal came to light when one of the victims spoke out in the media about the trauma she experienced.
A podcast series in 2022 then revealed the full extent of the campaign.
Henriette Berthelsen has called for a "Truth and Reconciliation" commission to be established. The Danish government is considering the idea.
According to the 68-year-old psychologist, that would make it possible to "acknowledge what happened".
"I believe that only then will we be able to begin to heal and move forward -- not as adversaries, but as human beings and as peoples equal in dignity."

Ecuador intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash
- Published
Ecuador's intelligence chief and his wife have been killed in a helicopter that crashed at Mount Ololokwe in central Kenya.
Michele Sensi-Contugi, 44, and his wife, fashion designer Stephany Hollihan, 42, were among the group of seven people - six tourists and the pilot - killed in Samburu county at approximately 09:13 (06:13 GMT) on Wednesday.
Five of victims were Americans, a US State Department spokesperson said. The Reuters news agency reports that Hollihan also held US citizenship.
The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority (KCAA) said the helicopter was on a scenic flight from a wildlife conservancy in Loisaba to Ewaso Nyiro, a river that flows along several national reserves.
Samburu county is a popular tourist destination with many private wildlife conservancies and is renowned for its stunning landscape.
Images from the scene show smoke at the wooded crash site on Mount Ololokwe, as members of the Kenya Red Cross approach the still-burning wreckage.
Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa named Sensi-Contugo director of the country's Centre of Strategic Intelligence (CIES) in January 2024.
The office of the president and Ecuador's National Assembly expressed their condolences over his death and that of Hollihan.
The Italian-Ecuadorean businessman had had close links to Noboa even before he was chosen to lead the intelligence service and was considered a close ally of the president.
Shortly before being named head of the CIES, he had served for four months as a minister in his cabinet.
Noboa has declared three days of national mourning starting on Thursday.
Newspapers in Ecuador have also run obituaries of Hollihan. The Guayaquil-based designer founded Sensi Studio, a brand praised for incorporating traditional Ecuadorean elements and materials in its designs.
Lady Lori Helicopters, which operated the Eurocopter EC130 B4 aircraft, said it was "deeply saddened" by the accident.
"Our deepest sympathies are with the guests, crew, their families and loved ones, and all those affected by this tragic accident," a statement read.
According to a memo seen by the BBC's US partner CBS News, external one of the Americans killed in the crash was NBCUniversal journalist José Alberto Suárez.
In the memo, NBCUniversal called Suárez "a deeply respected leader and beloved friend and colleague.
"José was an exceptional colleague and mentor to many," the memo read.
Miami restaurateur Roger Duarte was among the Americans killed in the crash, according to local and US media.
Commenting on his death on X, US Rep Carlos Antonio Gimenez wrote: "Our prayers are with their loved ones during this incredibly difficult time. May their memories be a blessing."
The other victims have not yet been identified.
Helicopter crashes are not uncommon in Kenya.
In February, a helicopter crash in the Rift Valley county of Nandi killed six people, including a member of parliament.
In 2024, the military chief, Gen Francis Omondi Ogolla, died after an army helicopter that was carrying 11 people crashed in the west of the country, with only two survivors.
In June 2021 at least 10 soldiers were killed when their helicopter crashed while landing near the capital, Nairobi.

Partey signs for Al-Shabab in Saudi Pro League

Saudi Pro League side Al-Shabab have confirmed the signing of Ghana international Thomas Partey.
The former Arsenal midfielder, who made 167 appearances for the Gunners between 2020 and 2025, became a free agent this summer when Villarreal decided against extending his expiring contract.
The 33-year-old is scheduled to stand trial next year after pleading not guilty to seven charges of rape and one count of sexual assault relating to allegations by four different women between 2020 and 2022.
During this summer's World Cup, Partey was denied entry to Canada before Ghana's opening match of the tournament against Panama because of ongoing criminal proceedings in the UK.
Partey wrongly told officials he had never been arrested or charged with a crime. He went on to play in Ghana's other three games at the tournament as they lost in the last 32 stage to Colombia.
Al-Shabab, whose squad contains former Burnley captain Josh Brownhill and ex-Wolves winger Daniel Podence, finished 13th last season in the Saudi Pro League and lost their opening match this term.

The marquee at Broadway‘s Booth Theatre appears to confirm the rumors: Bruce Norris‘ acclaimed and controversial play Downstate will take up residence at the venue in an upcoming production directed by Joe Mantello.
The news was first reported by the Chicago Tribune – the play premiered in 2018 at Chicago’s Steppenwolf Theatre Company – with the newspaper noting that the Broadway staging will be produced by Scott Rudin and feature at least two members of the original Chicago cast: Francis Guinan and K. Todd Freeman.
The Chicago staging was followed by an Off Broadway production at Playwrights Horizons in 2022. Both of those productions were directed by Pam MacKinnon, not Mantello.
The play, set in a group home for people convicted of sex crimes, received overwhelmingly positive reviews for the Off Broadway production, winning the 2023 New York Drama Critics’ Circle Award for Best Play.
Watch on Deadline
Specifically, the plot follows four men who have been convicted of sex offenses and have completed their prison sentences but remain on the sex offender registry and live in a group home in downstate Illinois. During the course of the play, one of the men is confronted by a former student.
The Rudin-Mantello pairing would reunite the two following their massively successful, Tony-winning 2026 revival of Death of a Salesman starring Nathan Lane and Laurie Metcalf. Rudin, Mantello and Metcalf also collaborated on Samuel D. Hunter’s play Little Bear Ridge Road last season following its premiere at Steppenwolf (the Chicago company did not participate in the Broadway staging of that play).
The Broadway premiere of Downstate has not been officially announced, and aside from the marquee lights no Downstate signage on the Booth is evident. Deadline has reached out to sources for confirmation of the plans.
The play, which has also been staged in the West End and Washington, D.C., came under fire from right-wing commentators and U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, who responded to a favorable review in the Washington Post by tweeting, “So now the corporate media is praising pedophilia.”
Norris, whose play Clybourne Park won the 2012 Tony Award for Best Play, responded to the controversy prior to its Off Broadway engagement in a statement quoted by Playbill: “A depiction of something is not an endorsement. But, I do think that witnessing the lives of characters on stage encourages identification, and if you spend two hours in the company of a group of sex offenders, do you emerge from the experience with your certainty about them momentarily disrupted? The goal is not to forgive, but rather to complicate an easy and casually cruel response.”
In addition to the New York Drama Critics’ Circle Award, the Off Broadway production won the Obie Award for Playwriting.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?
- Published
The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is now the deadliest of the 17 the country has faced as it continues to spread. United Nations experts have described it as the fastest growing outbreak on record in terms of new infections.
Getting the spread of the deadly virus under control is challenging because it involves a rare species of Ebola for which there is no vaccine - though some are being tested - and the epicentre is in an area affected by conflict.
What is Ebola and what are the symptoms?
Ebola is a rare but deadly disease caused by a virus.
Ebola viruses normally infect animals, typically fruit bats, but outbreaks among humans can sometimes start when people eat or handle infected animals.
It takes two to 21 days for symptoms to appear. They come on suddenly and start like the flu or malaria, with fever, headache and tiredness.
As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.
The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.
Ebola outbreaks used to be small and contained to remote rural areas. However, urbanisation is pushing larger populations closer to these natural reservoirs of Ebola and increasing the risk of transmission.
Why is this Ebola outbreak different and is there a vaccine?
This outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which had not been seen for over a decade.
Named after a district in Uganda where it was first detected, Bundibugyo has only caused two previous outbreaks - in 2007 and 2012.
One study showed that it killed about a third, external of those infected, far less than the more common Zaire (66.6%) and Sudan (48.5%) species. About 48% of those known to have been infected in the current outbreak have died.
Initial blood tests for Ebola in the affected areas were negative as they were designed to identify the more common form of the disease.
In July, the UK's medicines regulator, the MHRA, said it had given permission for the first human trials of a vaccine for Bundibugyo to go ahead.
It was created by a team from the University of Oxford based on the same technology used in the Oxford-AstraZeneca Covid vaccine.
It took scientists just eight weeks to develop the new jab after plugging in genetic code from the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.
The vaccine is being tested on 50 volunteers from Oxford aged 18 to 55 to see whether it triggers the correct antibody response without causing significant side effects.
Three other groups are also developing different vaccines for Bundibugyo although they have not yet entered clinical trials.
While treatments are available for other species of the Ebola virus, no drugs have been specifically approved to treat those infected with Bundibugyo.
DR Congo is currently preparing to roll out the Ervebo vaccine - which helps protect against the Zaïre species of Ebola - as part of a trial to see if it is effective against the Bundibugyo species.
The World Health Organization (WHO) is also sponsoring a separate clinical trial in the country to see whether two existing antiviral therapies can improve survival rates.
The two drugs selected as the most promising are an experimental monoclonal antibody called MBP134 and remdesivir, an injection into a vein, which is also used to treat Covid.
A further complication is that the outbreak is taking place in a conflict zone, with a quarter of million people displaced from their homes and people moving across porous borders into neighbouring countries.
How did the current Ebola outbreak start?
The first known case was a nurse who developed symptoms on 24 April, which means the virus had been spreading undetected for weeks.
The nurse died in Bunia, the capital of eastern DR Congo's Ituri province, according to Congolese Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba.
The victim's body was repatriated to Mongbwalu.
Kamba said one of the reasons the virus spread so quickly was the number of people exposed to the body during the funeral ceremony.
But researchers believe that it may have been spreading since February but it was initially misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid.
How many Ebola cases have been reported and where are they?
On 23 August, officials said there had been 5,514 confirmed cases and 2,642 confirmed deaths from the virus in DR Congo.
There have also been 1,200 recoveries from Ebola so far, including four nurses whose discharge from hospital was celebrated at a special ceremony.
Ituri province is the epicentre of this outbreak and accounts for the vast majority of confirmed infections.
Cases have also been confirmed in North Kivu (714) and South Kivu (3), provinces partly controlled by the rebel AFC-M23 alliance. These discoveries signalled the outbreak's spread from its epicentre.
The last patient being treated for Ebola in neighbouring Uganda was discharged from hospital on 16 July. Up to that point, the country had recorded 20 confirmed cases - with most having travelled from DR Congo - and two deaths.
Uganda has since announced it is Ebola-free, going against the protocol of waiting 42 days - until 27 August - from when the last patient recovers to declare an outbreak over.
What is being done in DR Congo to tackle the current Ebola outbreak?
Mass gatherings have been banned in the six provinces with confirmed cases - Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uele and Bas-Uele.
The capital city, Kinshasa - which has no confirmed cases and is located some 1,800 km (1,100) miles from the outbreak - has also been ordered to ban mass gatherings.
The government has now established four laboratories in Ituri - in Bunia, Mongbwalu, Beni and Aru - which can test blood samples for Bundibugyo and deliver results within 24 hours, removing earlier delays.
Surveillance systems, contact tracing and the treatment infrastructure, with dedicated centres in several affected towns, have also been expanded, according to the health minister.
The WHO has dedicated $3.9m (£2.9m) to tackling the outbreak, while Africa CDC has announced a $319m budget.
A toll-free number, 151, has been provided for reporting symptoms and people are being reminded to:
- avoid contact with bodies of people who died with symptoms, or with dead animals
- not eat raw meat, as undercooked food may transmit the virus
- practise social distancing.
How have the rebels responded to the latest Ebola outbreak?
The AFC-M23 group has created an Ebola response team in an effort to prevent transmissions in the areas it controls.
In late June, the rebel authorities had declared their zones Ebola-free, but introduced new restrictions in August, following two travellers testing positive in North Kivu.
Shared taxis and passenger boats between government-held and rebel-held areas of the province, have been suspended, highlighting the hostilities between the two sides.
The region's Ebola response co-ordinator Dr Freddy Kaniki, told the BBC in July that while UN agencies such as the WHO and Unicef - for children - had been helping, there has been no co-ordination with the Congolese government.

What are Rwanda and other countries doing about the Ebola outbreak?
Rwanda closed its borders with DR Congo earlier on in the outbreak. According to Congolese media, authorities began to reopen parts of the border late in June following a lull in local infections.
Uganda has temporarily suspended flights, buses and all other public transport crossing the border with DR Congo.
Several other African countries have tightened border screenings and bolstered health facilities.
The US has extended travel restrictions on its citizens who have been to DR Congo. Anyone who wants to return home must spend 21 days in a third country before being allowed into America.

Donald Trump announced Friday a new US oil agreement with Venezuela’s interim president Delcy Rodríguez, saying the US will have “majority” control of 65bn barrels of proven oil reserves.
The terms of the agreement remain to be seen, but the US president said on his social-media platform that it had been brokered “through a partnership with private business” by his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, and defense secretary, Pete Hegseth.
The administration, Trump wrote, has “secured majority U.S. control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer”.
Trump said the agreement would more than double American oil reserves.
“This deal is a huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people,” Rubio wrote on social media.
Trump’s announcement provided few details on the structure of the agreement, the fields or companies involved, or how the US would exercise majority control over the reserves.
Venezuela has an estimated 303bn barrels of proven oil reserves, the world’s largest.
Since the US captured and removed former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro from power in January, Washington has been trying to secure a stable flow of Venezuelan crude oil for US refineries while promoting American investment into the Opec country’s deteriorated energy industry, which produces 1.25m barrels per day of crude.
Trump is under pressure before November’s midterm elections over rising gasoline prices, which could be eased through cheaper oil supplies and expanded output.
The US also has been looking for solutions to replenish its strategic petroleum reserve, the oil stockpile, including the possibility of crude swaps with US producers.
Earlier this week, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Trump administration was “in advanced talks with Venezuela for the U.S. to take a direct stake in more than a dozen oilfields that house nearly one-third of the country’s massive energy reserves”. Axios also reported on the negotiations, quoting a US official who claimed the deal would be “massive”.
The discussion was reportedly over a US stake in Venezuela’s most promising oil-and-gasfields, with some 90bn barrels of proven reserves.
The reports caused unease and anger among members of Venezuela’s opposition, who are already up in arms about Trump’s failure to bring about genuine political change after capturing Maduro.
“It’s a land grab – a massive land grab,” said one well-known opposition figure who asked not to be named because of the sensitivities of criticizing the US. “It’s revolting because this is not the United States one would have [expected]. This is not the United States of the Marshall plan. This is a rapacious, mafioso United States.”
The announcement comes as Chevron and other US energy companies are expected to sign a deal next week investing billions in Venezuela’s oil fields, according to the Journal.
Tom Phillips and Reuters contributed reporting

Zerodha’s core business is no longer growing. Regulatory curbs and changing investor behaviour are cooling trading activity and squeezing brokerage revenue. Broking revenue fell 10.4% from ₹3,066 Cr in FY25 to ₹2,738 Cr in FY26. Net transaction charges (income earned from exchange-related transaction fee rebates) also fell to zero from ₹400 Cr in FY25 due to SEBI’s true-to-label norm framework. In a blog post, CEO Nithin Kamath hinted that its overall top line remained almost flat in FY26 versus ₹8,847 Cr a fiscal year ago. Despite the revenue squeeze, Zerodha kept its bottom line largely intact, with profit rising marginally to ₹4,283 Cr in FY26 from ₹4,231 Cr in FY25. So, with its core revenue engine slowing, what is keeping Zerodha’s profits afloat? The answer: Zerodha is increasingly making money from sources other than brokerage. Interest income (₹2,269 Cr): The discount broker earns interest on its cash balances and other interest-generating assets. Delayed payment charges + MTF (₹448 Cr): It earns money when customers delay paying for trades and, through MTF, when customers borrow money to buy stocks. AMC charges: Zerodha’s asset management business is also generating more fee income, though it is still relatively small. In Q1 FY27, the discount broker said that nearly 40% of its gross revenue came from the businesses outside its core trading platform. While these revenue streams are cushioning the impact of falling brokerage income, are they large enough to replace the core business entirely, especially when its arch-rival Groww now has an active client base almost twice the size? Zerodha’s User Problem Is Bigger Than It Looks Regulatory changes have added to the pressure on Zerodha’s core brokerage business, particularly by curbing derivatives and currency trading activity. SEBI’s derivatives clampdown and RBI’s tighter rules around currency futures and options (F&O), introduced in 2024, reduced trading activity across segments. According to Zerodha, these regulatory changes led to a 20-30% drop in F&O activity across exchanges and brokers. INR currency F&O volumes fell 90% after the RBI introduced rules requiring trades to be backed by an underlying foreign currency exposure. But regulations do not fully explain the divergence between Zerodha and Groww, which has almost twice as many clients as Zerodha. In July, Groww added 70,119 active clients, taking its base to 13.12 Mn and its NSE market share to 28.88%. Zerodha lost 38,725 clients, leaving it with 6.76 Mn and a 14.88% share. The entire broking industry added only around 8,000 net active clients during the month. The divergence is visible in revenue as well. Groww’s operating revenue rose from ₹ 2,609 Cr in FY24 to ₹4,645 Cr in FY26, an increase of about 78%. Zerodha, by comparison, saw its revenue decline from nearly ₹9,994 Cr in FY24 to around ₹8,847 Cr in FY26. However, according to Rahul Sharma, head of office research at Equity99, Groww and Zerodha are not competing for the same customer or the same kind of revenue. While Groww has focused more on mass-market equity, mutual funds and SIPs, Zerodha continues to derive a significant portion of its revenue from active F&O traders. Even CEO Nithin Kamath argues that the active-client market is not the most important metric. This, however, does not answer the fundamental question: if Zerodha is not trying to win on users, can it extract enough value from its existing base? MTF Rescue Boat Margin trading facility (MTF) is helping Zerodha build a new revenue stream, but it is not the only one trying to reduce its dependence on trading-led revenue. Angel One has been moving aggressively in the same direction, with client funding, wealth management, asset management and distribution becoming a larger part of its business. Zerodha launched its MTF offering in December 2024, after years of debating whether to enter the segment. At the time, Zerodha said it made little business sense to remain the only large broker without the product. The product has since scaled. Zerodha’s MTF book has reached around ₹9,000 Cr, with customers borrowing about ₹6,000 Cr. Per Kamath, MTF contributes roughly 10% of the startup’s revenue. The financials show the change clearly. Delayed payment charges and MTF generated ₹448 Cr in FY26, compared with ₹22 Cr in FY25. The reason this matters is simple: Brokerage revenue depends heavily on customers trading. MTF allows Zerodha to earn interest from customers who borrow to invest, creating a revenue stream that is less dependent on the number of trades. The bigger issue is that MTF is being built against a business that remains heavily exposed to derivatives. Avinash Gorakhshar, founder of Avinash Mentor Research, said continued regulatory pressure on F&O could make Zerodha’s slower diversification into mass-market wealth products a growth constraint. But MTF is not yet large enough to replace the revenue lost from Zerodha’s traditional business. It puts Zerodha in an interesting position. Angel One, which had a broadly similar active client base to Zerodha at the end of FY26, has also been building its client funding business; its average client funding book stood at ₹5,305 Cr for FY26 and rose to ₹6,783 Cr by June 2026. It is pertinent to note that Angel One’s client funding book includes MTF loans and period-end trade receivables, net of non-interest-bearing receivables. Then there is also a limit to how aggressively Zerodha can push the product. Kamath has acknowledged the risks associated with leveraged investing and said the startup does not want to encourage customers to borrow simply because it generates revenue. The Diversification Dilemma Zerodha remains profitable, its AMC is scaling faster than Groww's AUM, and its MTF book has grown rapidly. But the timing of some of these moves is tricky. Zerodha had a significant first-mover advantage in digital broking, but MTF came only in late 2024, while it launched AMC in 2023. It is now bringing mutual fund transactions to Kite, after keeping the trading and mutual fund experience separate for years. The gap is more visible in wealth management. Groww has moved into the affluent investor segment through W, its wealth management platform, which offers access to Portfolio Management Services (PMS), Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and private market opportunities. Lalit Keshre’s Groww entered the segment after acquiring Fisdom in October last year, a deal that brought wealth management and distribution capabilities into its business. Zerodha, by comparison, remains largely a self-directed investment platform through Kite and Coin. Its Zerodha Fund House gives it an asset management business, but that is different from offering personalised wealth management. However, not everyone believes Zerodha’s slower customer growth means it has been slow to respond to changing market realities. Sharma of Equity99 argues that the startup is making a deliberate trade-off, prioritising profitability and capital efficiency over aggressive customer acquisition. But with Groww moving faster into wealth and adjacent products, Zerodha risks falling behind if its diversification does not scale quickly enough. All in all, Zerodha is not a troubled business. It remains highly profitable, has a strong brand, a sizeable customer base and growing businesses beyond brokerage. But the economics of digital broking are changing, and the company can no longer rely on its traditional F&O-heavy model to drive growth. Therefore, it will have to diversify fast enough before its core business shrinks further. Edited By Shishir Parasher Creatives: Varshita Srivastava

Srinagar, Aug 30: Apni Party President Syed Mohammad Altaf Bukhari on Sunday urged the people of Srinagar’s Shehr-e-Khaas not to fall prey to the decades-long exploitation by traditional political parties like the National Conference. He called upon them to become aware of their political and democratic rights and assert them to bring about a change in their present difficult situation.
He was addressing a workers’ convention in Habba Kadal, Srinagar, which was attended by a large gathering of local residents and party workers.
Addressing the gathering, Bukhari expressed serious concern over the continued poor condition of Srinagar city and the hardships faced by its residents. He said that to change this situation, people must take responsibility and stop falling prey to the exploitative politics of the National Conference and its leadership.
He said, “Marhoom Sheikh Sahib successfully earned the unconditional loyalty of the people of the city and built a political empire for generations of his family. However, this blind following by the people paved the way for a prolonged lack of development and prosperity in the city. Even today, decades later, people continue to blindly follow the party, often at the cost of their own future and that of the coming generations.”
He went on to say, “There are around nine lakh people living in this historic city, yet a large number of them are struggling even for basic amenities. Look at the plight of our youth. They are educated but remain jobless, with many forced to take up petty jobs, like working as street vendors. How long can this situation continue?”
“Unfortunately, the existing reservation policy has also adversely affected the people of the city by further reducing employment opportunities for local youth. The residents of the city do not fall under any reserved category, except the Economically Weaker Section (EWS), whose reservation has also been reduced from 10 percent to 3 percent,” he added.
He went on to say, “This beautiful and historic city still lacks even basic amenities, like drinking water. There is a serious shortage of housing, and livelihood opportunities. Many of our daughters in the city, despite having crossed marriageable age, are unable to get married because of the severe financial difficulties faced by their families.”
“We must seriously think about how to change this pathetic situation. The first step is for the people to distance themselves from the political forces that have kept them in this condition despite receiving their support for decades,” he added.
Apni Party president said that by continuing to support the NC, the people of the city are, in fact, compromising their own interests and development.
He said, “Why don’t you understand this simple fact? Despite remaining in power for decades, this party allowed the city to remain in such a pathetic condition and, even worse, damaged its natural infrastructure.”
“Take Nallah Mar, for instance. It was an ancient waterway that connected Dal Lake and the Brari Nambal lagoon with the River Jhelum and Anchar Lake. Filling up this historic canal was one of the greatest acts of damage inflicted on this city and its people. It not only destroyed an important part of Srinagar’s natural drainage and waterway system but also robbed the city of a vital part of its historical heritage,” he said.
Remembering the days when Kashmiri Pandits and Muslims lived together in harmony in the city, Bukhari said, “I vividly remember the days when, as children, we used to attend tuition classes taught by some of the finest Pandit teachers. I also fondly remember the time when Muslims and Kashmiri Pandits lived together happily and prosperously, sharing a bond of mutual respect, trust, and brotherhood.”
Making a heartfelt appeal to the Kashmiri Pandit community, he said, “I urge my Kashmiri Pandit brethren to return so that, together, we can rediscover the past glory of our beautiful shared culture and work towards restoring peace, prosperity, and harmony.”
Apni Party President urged the people of the city to remain vigilant and ensure that, whenever the ULB polls are held, they vote wisely and choose their representatives thoughtfully, so that their developmental issues are addressed effectively.
He also urged the people to support Apni Party to enable it to implement its pro-people manifesto in the city and ensure sustained prosperity and development in this historic and beautiful city.
Speaking on the occasion, former Cabinet Minister and Apni Party Senior Vice President Ghulam Hassan Mir said that the “people of Srinagar city are facing severe hardships due to inadequate housing, limited livelihood opportunities, and a lack of developmental infrastructure.”
He said that “even the Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC) does not allow people to construct houses or commercial establishments on their own land, causing them further hardship and inconvenience.”
He said, “It is painful to see our youth struggling today. They do not have enough job opportunities, and many of them also face problems in getting passports and completing verification processes for jobs and passports.”
Lashing out at the government Mir said, “These people have placed their trust in you, given you their mandate, and voted you to power. How can a government refuse to address the issues and concerns of the very people who elected it?”
Party’s Provincial president Mohammad Ashraf Mir addressed the occasion and urged the people of the city to support Apni Party.
He said, “Unlike the traditional parties, this party does not belong to any family or any individual. This party belongs to people and its primary agenda is to serve the people. I urge you to make this party strengthen so that it will be able to implement its agenda for peace, prosperity and development of Jammu and Kashmir and its people.”
Besides Syed Mohammad Altaf Bukhari and Ghulam Hassan Mir, the prominent party leaders who spoke in the convention or who were present on the occasion included party’s Vice President Haji Mohammad Syed Akhoon, Provincial President Kashmir Mohammad, Chief Spokesperson & State Secretary Muntazir Mohiudin, District President Srinagar & Constituency In-charge Central Shaltang Zaffar Habib, Provincial Secretary Kashmir Malik Aftab, Provincial Secretary Kashmir Peer Wajahat, Provincial Joint Secretary Kashmir & Constituency In-charge Habba Kadal Jeelani Hamid Kumar, Provincial Joint Secretary Aamir Ashraf Bhat, Provincial Joint Secretary Kashmir Aijaz Rather, Organiser Central Kashmir Mohammad Shafi Mir, Vice President Srinagar Mohsin Zaffar Shah, Provincial Youth President Kashmir Jibran Dar, Joint Secretary District Srinagar Khursheed Ahmad Makhdoomi, Joint Secretary District Srinagar Sameer Ahmad Lone, Constituency In-charge Khanyar Amir Bhat, and others.

Fighting to stay No 1 - Sabalenka's US Open mission
- Published
All was bright in Aryna Sabalenka's world when she completed a rare 'Sunshine Double' earlier this season.
Becoming only the fifth woman to win the Indian Wells and Miami titles back-to-back, Sabalenka emphasised her position as the dominant player on the WTA Tour and created a 3,000-point lead at the top of the world rankings.
But a difficult period quickly followed - seemingly out of nowhere - leaving the 28-year-old Belarusian clinging on to her position going into the US Open, which starts on Sunday.
Two-time defending champion Sabalenka returns to New York with a 17-7 win-loss record since the Miami triumph, including a chastening French Open quarter-final exit and a disheartening defeat in the Wimbledon fourth round.
It is a record far below the four-time major winner's lofty standards.
With 2,000 points to defend at Flushing Meadows and Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina now trailing by only 434, Sabalenka must win again to extend her 99-week run as the world number one.
Asked if she felt confident she can rediscover her mojo on the hard courts on which she has thrived, Sabalenka said: "Absolutely. These tough lessons are definitely going to make me way, way stronger and working even harder."

Sabalenka's four Grand Slam singles titles - two Australian Open and two US Open triumphs, all on hard courts - are more than most players can dream of.
However, she has also lost four major finals and six semi-finals, despite a consistency on the biggest stages that is unrivalled among her peers.
The concern in recent months has been Sabalenka's mental focus disappearing in less pressurised situations.
This was most recently apparent in her Cincinnati Open fourth-round defeat by 20-year-old Czech opponent Sara Bejlek. Sabalenka led 5-1 in a first-set tie-break and 4-1 in the second set, but continued to lack composure in the rallies as Bejlek rallied to win 7-6 (9-7) 6-4.
At her previous tournament in Toronto, she lost to Russian world number 19 Ekaterina Alexandrova in the last 16 as her serve crumbled.
During the clay-court swing, Sabalenka capitulated after winning the first set against Hailey Baptiste in Madrid, Sorana Cirstea in Rome and, most notably, Diana Shnaider at Roland Garros.
"I work on my mental side of the game. I've been trying to reset my mind and to come back stronger," a bullish Sabalenka said in New York.
"It's only a matter of time for me to come back."
Who could take Sabalenka's crown?
The drop-off in Sabalenka's results have opened the door for Rybakina, who beat the Belarusian to win the Australian Open in January, to take over as world number one.
Rybakina might not even have to win a match at Flushing Meadows to do that, as she has fewer ranking points to defend than Sabalenka.
However, there are questions over her fitness because of an ankle injury sustained in the Cincinnati quarter-finals.
Rybakina can secure the number one ranking if her nearest rivals - Sabalenka, Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff - do not win the title.
If Sabalenka does retain the title, Rybakina would still also rise to the top by reaching the semi-finals.
Pegula, 32, has been ultra-consistent for several seasons without landing a major title, but the 2024 finalist hopes her runs to the Washington and Cincinnati finals will provide the platform for another crack at her home Slam.
Gauff, who beat Pegula to the Cincinnati trophy last week, already has the experience of winning in New York after claiming her first major there in 2023.
Twelve months ago, the 22-year-old American's game was clouded by uncertainty but returns with more confidence and fluidity in her serve.
Beneath the leading quartet, the rest of the top 10 also hold either a Grand Slam or WTA 1,000 title - a group led by French Open winner Mirra Andreeva, Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and six-time major winner Iga Swiatek.
"You can just see how the depth is pretty crazy," said Pegula.

For the third Grand Slam in a row, the rivalry between Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz has been put on hold.
The pair swept all eight major titles between them in 2024 and 2025, with Alcaraz extending that run with victory at this year's Australian Open.
But the pair have not competed at the same Grand Slam since.
Alcaraz missed the French Open and Wimbledon with a wrist injury, and makes his comeback from a four-month absence in New York.
A day after the 23-year-old Spaniard announced his plan to return, Sinner revealed he had been ruled out with a knee issue.
"It's kind of weird. We are not going see each other for, like, six months now, seven months," said Alcaraz.
Sinner's absence and the uncertainty around Alcaraz's fitness will galvanise the rest of the chasing pack - particularly 39-year-old Novak Djokovic.
The Serb great, a 24-time Grand Slam champion, insists he has not put an "expiry date" on his extraordinary career. He continues to put himself in the mix for titles as he looks to finally land a standalone record 25th victory which would move him clear of Australia's Margaret Court on the all-time list.
He has reached at least the semi-finals in six of the past seven Slams, but has not gone all the way since triumphing at the 2023 US Open.
Germany's Alexander Zverev leads the seedings as he looks to reach a third straight major final, having won his first Slam at the French Open before losing to Sinner at Wimbledon.

There are a few questions in my household that irritate me more than "What's for dinner?"
I think it's the casual assumption that I have created a meal plan for the week, done all the food shopping and prep, and gotten dinner on the table at exactly the time everyone wants it, all while trying to accommodate my kids' likes and dislikes. Not to mention the cleanup after.
We are a family of four, and just the idea of "What's for dinner?" can be exhausting. Every parent deals with this every night, but that doesn't make it any less of a pain in the butt, even when my husband helps out.
I tried a meal subscription plan
This past spring, I was at peak meal-planning-overwhelm, when I remembered I'd gotten a card in the mail offering a discount if I signed up for a particular meal delivery subscription — one that we had used in the past right after my second kid was born — but hadn't tried in years. "Their food was pretty good," I mused to myself. The wheels started turning, and the next thing I knew, I had signed the family up for two meals a week.
The impact was immediate and incredible — for me, at least. Just having those two nights a week covered for dinner made such a huge difference in my mental load.
Deciding what to eat is what bothered me the most
Grocery shopping was not my main inconvenience; it was deciding what to have for dinner each night, and then all the prep work. It felt like I was wasting so much mental energy on what we should have, did we have that too recently to have it again this week, does one child hate it so much that she won't eat it even though the other child loves it, and so on.
I could do more than two days a week, but then the service starts getting pricey for our budget.
Another thing I love is that meal delivery lets me try recipes I wouldn't usually make. If a recipe calls for spices or sauces I don't typically have in my kitchen, I find I'm less inclined to make it. But when every ingredient is sent to me in the exact amount needed, I'm all in.
I am not a gourmet chef. I do not toil over recipes of my own invention until I've perfected them. But I do know how to follow a recipe and cook the basics, and the meal delivery services I've tried make it even easier. Each recipe gives you step-by-step instructions and the exact amount of every ingredient. And if you can't stand cooking, some services offer pre-made meals that just need to be heated up.
These days, I am no longer irritated when someone asks, "What's for dinner?" I simply say, "Chicken burrito bowls," or "Pork stir fry with lettuce cups," and go on my merry way.
Do both kids love every meal every time? Absolutely not. But the subscription has lots of options every week, so I can easily find meals that work for everyone most of the time. Then I find it much less daunting to have a meal plan for the remaining nights of the week. And that to me is worth its weight in gold.

Whisper it quietly, but certain bricks in Apple’s walled garden might be getting taken away.
Thanks to some recent upgrades added to Android by Google, it's now easier than ever to share files between an iPhone and an Android phone, without installing any new apps (though that's still an option too).
So if you need to send a photo, contact card, web link, or anything else, these are the options you have available. As is often the case with Android, they may vary depending on the make and model of your handset, though you should find at least one of these methods works for you.
Share Files via AirDrop
This is the big one: Google recently figured out a way to add support for AirDrop—Apple's previously closed-off, device-to-device sharing protocol—to newer Pixel phones. It doesn't appear that Apple was involved in the process, but the company hasn't gotten in Google's way since, and the functionality has been rolled out to other phones (including the recent Pixel and Galaxy handsets).
Some prep work may be required. On Samsung phones, you need to open Settings, then choose Connected devices > Quick Share and enable Share with Apple devices—though there's no such toggle switch on Pixel phones—it'll just work right away. It needs enabling on iOS too: From Settings, tap General > AirDrop, and Everyone for 10 Minutes.
With that done, whenever you tap the share button anywhere in any Android app, you can choose Quick Share from the resulting pop-up panel to communicate with a nearby iPhone. The iPhone should show up in the available devices, so select it to start the transfer—which will still need to be accepted on the iPhone.
It will work the other way too, starting from AirDrop on an iPhone, as long as the Android device is set up to receive from any other device. From Settings, tap either Connection preferences (Google Pixel phones) or Connected devices (Samsung Galaxy phones), then select Quick Share > Who can share with you.
Share Files via QR code
Google hasn't stopped with AirDrop on Android. It has also recently pushed out a QR-code-based option for sharing from Android to iOS. It's a bit more clunky than AirDrop, but it'll work no matter what kind of Android phone you've got.
Again, you need to go through Quick Share, which pops up as an option whenever you try to share something in Android—no matter what the app or item you want to share. You won't see an iPhone appear if you don't have the AirDrop functionality, but you should see a Use QR code option on the right, under Share with iPhone and other devices, which after a few moments shrinks down to just a QR code symbol.
Tap this option to get your QR code on screen. On the iPhone side, AirDrop still needs enabling (via General > AirDrop > Everyone for 10 Minutes), and the iPhone camera can then be pointed at the QR code to get to a special Google web address. That will lead to a simple download page for the shared file or content.
Google says transferred files remain in the cloud for 24 hours, after which they'll be securely deleted. They don't count toward your Google Drive storage quota, and you can share up to 1,000 files in a single session, to a maximum of 20 iPhones (or iPads or Macs, which also support AirDrop).
Other Sharing Options
You do have a multitude of sharing options to pick from if you want to get something from Android to iOS. You can simply attach a file to an email, for example, or use a messaging app that supports both Android and iOS, like WhatsApp. Bear in mind that certain messaging apps compress photos and videos before sending, though many apps let you turn compression off in the settings.
Cloud storage apps are another helpful method you can use, though as with messaging apps you want something that works well on any platform (so not iCloud). Google Drive and Dropbox are two apps that are simple to use, run well on Android and iOS, and have smart sharing features built in, for example.
For iPhone-to-iPhone and Android-to-Android connections and file transfers, everything is much more straightforward: You can just use AirDrop or Quick Share through the relevant share panels, and the receiving device should pop up (assuming you've set the right availability options, as described above).
One option you can't use is Bluetooth: Apple locks down Bluetooth on the iPhone to some extent, so while you can connect accessories like wireless earbuds, you can't use it for wireless file transfers.

13-year-old among 321 arrested as Hong Kong police seize drugs worth HK$130m
19 boys and nine girls under the age of 18 among those taken into custody during seven-week citywide crackdown
Hong Kong police have arrested 321 people, including a 13-year-old, and seized HK$130 million (US$16.5 million) worth of suspected illegal drugs during a seven-week citywide crackdown.
Code-named “Tailbacker”, the operation ran from July 12 to August 29, and uncovered 234 drug-related cases, police said on Sunday.
The 321 suspects, aged between 13 and 72, comprised 228 men, 65 women and 28 minors. They were arrested for suspected offences that included the manufacturing, possession, and trafficking of dangerous drugs, as well as operating a drug den and possessing Part 1 poisons. Some have already been formally charged.
The underage suspects comprised 19 boys and nine girls, all under the age of 18.
Over the course of the operation, officers seized 231kg (509 lbs) of suspected illegal drugs with a market value of HK$130 million, including 76kg of cocaine, 65kg of ketamine, 3.7 litres of liquid etomidate, and 6,400 etomidate vape pods, as well as some heroin, cannabis and methamphetamine.
Police noted a significant increase in etomidate seizures compared with similar operations last year.

Srinagar, Aug 30: The Jammu and Kashmir unit of the BJP on Sunday hit out at Kashmir's chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq for urging political parties to unite for the restoration of Article 370, claiming that such statements are attempts to provoke the public and disrupt the peaceful atmosphere that has emerged in the valley after years of violence.
BJP spokesperson Altaf Thakur said Parliament took a "historic" constitutional decision on August 5, 2019, and the Supreme Court subsequently upheld the abrogation of Article 370.
"Mirwaiz Umar Farooq should understand that Article 370 is not coming back. Parliament has buried Article 370 forever, and no political party, leader or pressure group can reverse that constitutional reality," Thakur said.
He said such calls risked dragging Kashmir back into the politics of the past.
"Statements of this nature are meant to provoke people and vitiate the peaceful atmosphere in the Valley once again. This will never be allowed. The nation has paid a very heavy price for the return of peace to Kashmir. The sacrifices of our brave security forces and civilians, including political workers who laid down their lives for peace and democracy, cannot be allowed to be undermined or challenged through politically motivated statements," Thakur said.
He noted that Kashmir has experienced enough bloodshed, shutdowns, stone-pelting, and disruption, and that the people should not be pushed into another cycle of instability.
"Those who attempt to revive old fault lines must understand that Kashmir has moved ahead. Our youth want education, employment, entrepreneurship, investment, tourism and opportunities. They do not want to return to an era when shutdown calendars dictated their lives and violence dictated the future," he said.
Thakur mentioned that political parties were free to express their views within the constitutional framework, but attempts to create agitation around an issue that had already been constitutionally settled would serve no purpose.
"Democracy gives everyone the right to speak and participate, but democracy cannot be reduced to repeatedly demanding the reversal of a constitutional decision that has already been upheld by the highest court of the country," he said.
On the issue of statehood, Thakur said the BJP has made its position clear that it would be restored at an appropriate time.
"There is a clear distinction between statehood and Article 370. Statehood will be restored at an appropriate time, as has been stated by the Government. But there is absolutely no question of bringing back Article 370," he said. Those spreading confusion on this issue should stop misleading the people," he said.

India began its Women’s Asia Cup 2026 campaign with a thumping 94-run win over Thailand at the Dubai International Stadium on Sunday.
Shafali Verma struck her 19th T20I half-century before the Indian bowlers, led by all-rounder Deepti Sharma, wrapped up a facile victory.
Chasing 160, the Thai were bundled out for just 65 in 16.1 overs, with wicketkeeper-batter Nannapat Koncharoenkai waging a lone battle with her 48-ball 41.
Deepti was undoubtedly the pick of the bowlers for the Women in Blue. The Agra player marked her 150th T20I with a double-wicket maiden, removing Naomi Hamilton and Nannaphat Chaihan in the ninth over. She ended her 1.1-over spell with three wickets and didn’t concede any runs.
Pacers Nandni Sharma (3/18), Kranti Gaud (1/26), and left-arm spinner N. Shree Charani (2/10 in three overs) were also amongst the wickets.
However, the Thailand side did have the Women in Blue in a spot of bother earlier in the match.
After losing the toss, openers Smriti Mandhana and Shafali got the three-time champion off to a flying start before the former was run out by a direct throw.
Debutant Pratika Rawal hit an 18-ball 22, adding 53 runs for the second wicket with Shafali, before departing. India found itself at 108/3 in 11.3 overs — skipper Harmanpreet Kaur had just mistimed a shot and gotten out on five — before it lost six wickets for just 29 runs.
Suleeporn Laomi was the chief architect of India’s batting collapse after the leg-spinner removed Shafali and big-hitter Richa Ghosh on consecutive deliveries in the 13th over. Pacer Chanida Sutthiruang restricted the run flow with an economical 1/14 in three overs.
But an unbeaten eight-ball 15 from Kranti made sure India crossed the 150-run mark and posted a total that would have been out of Thailand’s reach.

I’ve been reviewing laptops for well over a decade, sometimes testing more than 30 devices per year. They aren’t all winners, and many should be avoided, no matter how slick the marketing or cheap the discount. Good news: It’s my job to recommend laptops that fit your budget and won’t make you regret your purchase six months later. These are my favorite laptops that I’ve tested myself and would highly recommend you buy.
For more guidance, also see my recommendations in specific categories, such as the Best MacBooks, Best Gaming Laptops, Best Chromebooks, Best Budget Laptops, Best Windows Laptops, and Best 2-in-1 Laptops. My guide on How to Choose a Laptop may also help if you’re undecided.
Updated August 2026: I’ve updated my recommendations after testing the Dell XPS 13, Alienware 15 Gaming Laptop, and Lenovo LOQ 15 Essential.
The Laptops I Recommend Most
When friends or family ask what laptop to buy, I always start with the MacBook Air. It is far more powerful than its compact size suggests. It’s a shame about the recent $200 price increase from $1,099 to $1,299, but even at that new price, it remains my top pick because it nails the big picture. Everything from the trackpad to the speakers is of the highest quality, and it delivers all the performance and battery life the average person needs.
With the latest M5 chip, its GPU matches the M3 Pro MacBook Pro, easily handling everything from gaming to video editing. That’s not at all what the MacBook Air is designed for, but the performance is there when you want to dabble. It’s what makes it feel like a do-it-all machine, all contained in a fanless chassis that’s still one of the thinnest laptops you can buy. Oh, and did I mention it’ll last well over a full workday away from the wall socket and perform just as well on battery as when plugged in? In almost every aspect, it’s the gold standard.
While the lower price of the new MacBook Neo might be tempting, the MacBook Air is the better choice for anyone working at a computer all day. With its superior performance, extra memory, faster storage, and Thunderbolt ports, you will never have to question if you have the right tool for the job. (And unless you already know you need a MacBook Pro, you probably don’t.)
Speaking of price, I have to mention the new Dell XPS 13 next. It's primarily being talked about as a budget laptop, thanks to its $699 starting configuration. But that model only comes with 8 GB of RAM, which presented some performance limitations when I tested it. Dell, fortunately, sells an upgrade model with 16 GB of RAM for $899, which is otherwise identical. Both models have the same gorgeous screen, which is not only sharp, bright, and color-accurate, but also includes a 120-Hz refresh rate, which makes animation and motion on the device look super smooth. The XPS 13 is filled with features like that, which don't normally end up in a laptop at this price.
While it doesn't have what I'd call powerhouse performance, the Intel Wildcat Lake chip inside gets the job done. Don't try to play games on it, though. That translates to great, all-day battery life, competitive with the MacBook Air. The XPS 13 is especially good for those who want a compact laptop. Because of the tiny bezels, it's still one of the best laptops to work on a plane with. But even beyond that, it's just the best laptops you can buy under $1,000 right now. You'll probably just want to avoid that 8 GB model. Beyond the memory situation, the only real caveat is the lack of a headphone jack.
If you want a Windows laptop that looks and feels high-end, I would point you to the OmniBook Ultra 14. It might be the prettiest Windows laptop you can buy right now. The device is beautifully built and incredibly sturdy, with a thin chassis, an oversized haptic trackpad, and polished metal edges. I also appreciate the three Thunderbolt 4 ports split between both sides for convenient charging, as well as the surprisingly good speakers. I tested the high-end model, which features a fast Snapdragon X2 Elite, 32 GB of RAM, and a gorgeous 2880 x 1800 OLED display. The screen offers near-perfect colors, excellent brightness, and astounding HDR performance. It doesn’t get much better than this. It's usually quite expensive, but we're finally starting to seem discounts that drop it to a more reasonable price. There's also an Intel model with a very efficient and powerful chip that would also be a good choice. I'd go with whichever is cheaper at the current moment.
And lastly, for something with a larger screen, I'd recommend the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x. It serves as a particularly good alternative to the 15-inch MacBook Air, coming in at a much lower cost. These days, you can buy the upgraded model with the 2560 x 1600 OLED display (and 165-Hz refresh rate) for $1,000, on sale at Amazon. While it's slightly thicker than the MacBook Air, it leaves more room for extra ports including HDMI, UBS-A, and an SD card slot. And while the Snapdragon X2 Plus isn’t quite an M5 killer, I was happy with the performance and battery life provided.
Cheap Laptops That Are Actually Good
While “cheap” means something different to everyone, the best budget laptops generally fall under $750. This is where Windows truly shines, offering great specs for less money. Thanks to the latest processors from Qualcomm and Intel, these laptops now offer battery life that rivals Apple. The best affordable laptop I’ve checked out is the HP OmniBook 5. The model I tested has a Snapdragon X processor, 16 GB of RAM, 512 GB of storage, and a 14-inch OLED screen. Discounts fluctuate frequently, but right now you can buy that configuration directly from HP for $650. That’s a killer deal.
I also recently tested the new HP OmniBook 3, which uses the same chip as the OmniBook 5. It frequently sells for less than the OmniBook 5 by at least a $100 or so. HP is selling this configuration of the 14-inch model for just $543. While the OmniBook 3 is a good alternative, the OmniBook 5 is much thinner and looks more modern. Neither laptop has a particularly great touchpad, though, which is easily the biggest flaw in both laptops. Between the two, the OmniBook 5 is the better buy if you can afford it.
The MacBook Neo is Apple’s new entry-level laptop. It initially started at an aggressive $599, but that price has recently been raised to $699. Even at that price, the laptop shines when it comes to the display. It offers the best screen you can find at this price, bringing the macOS experience to an unprecedented value, even at $699 (or $799 for the 512 GB model). Apple clearly gave priority to the front-of-screen experience, delivering a premium feel across the display, build quality, and keyboard. While the 8 GB of RAM, outdated ports, and slower SSD are notable drawbacks—making the MacBook Air a better choice for remote workers—the Neo is the most premium-feeling laptop available for students, travelers, and casual users.
Given how good some of these budget laptops are, it’s a bit harder to find a place for Chromebooks. The standout option is still the Lenovo Chromebook Plus 14. It’s the most premium Chromebook available, with an OLED screen, 16 GB of RAM, and battery life that rivals the MacBook Neo. Its price just keeps going up, though, now up to $849. That’s far too expensive for what you get.
Instead, I recommend the Acer Chromebook Plus 516, which is the best of the cheaper Chromebooks. While it’s a bit thick and the screen isn’t the sharpest (especially for a 16-inch laptop), it’s the best laptop you can buy for under $500, and it occasionally dips down to $349. Acer didn’t skimp on the quality of the touchpad, either, which I appreciate. Windows laptops are about to get much stronger in this category, however, just as higher-priced Chromebooks will be seemingly phased out over time and replaced by the upcoming Googlebooks. Personally, I wouldn't spend more than $500 for a Chromebook and would instead opt for one of the cheaper HP OmniBooks mentioned above if you're already spending close to this price.
Powerful Laptops for Those Who Need It
While the laptops above are great for the average person, content creators and gamers need extra performance. For the former, the 16-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro is the ultimate choice. It combines immense power with surprising portability and fantastic battery life—a rare feat. The M5 generation is the most impressive yet, with a greatly expanded GPU and significantly boosted on-device AI processing thanks to a more efficient Neural Engine and faster memory bandwidth. While it is one of the most powerful AI laptops available, the MacBook Pro isn’t for everyone; it is built specifically for professional creatives and engineers running heavy, demanding applications. It’s become more expensive in 2026, but there’s still nothing quite like it on the market.
There are a number of Windows alternatives to the MacBook Pro, including the Asus ProArt P16 and Lenovo Yoga Pro 9i. And while these are both powerful, they take an old-school approach to performance, using hot-and-heavy discrete graphics cards that significantly reduce the battery life to achieve that level of performance. We'll probably need to wait for Nvidia's anticipated RTX Spark laptops for a true MacBook Pro competitor later this year. The Dell XPS 14 takes a different approach, ditching the discrete GPU for Intel’s new X7 or X9 chip (also known as B390 or Intel Arc graphics). The results are seriously impressive, replicating the performance of an RTX 4050 without the downsides of using a discrete GPU. Moreover, the Dell XPS 14 has a level of polish in its design really seen only on MacBooks—even surpassing them in some areas. The more affordable configurations with the Core Ultra 5 or 7 don't have as strong of graphics, but you still get the premium design and excellent battery life.
The most common use for laptop performance, however, is for playing games. If you plan on booting up any graphically intensive games more than a couple of times a week, you will want a dedicated gaming laptop. After testing dozens over the past year, the Alienware 15 Gaming Laptop is my current recommendation. At $1,200 for the RTX 5050 model or $1,350 for the upgrade RTX 5060, this is the best deal in gaming laptops right now.
It performs well, though its strongest quality compared to the competition is how robust and beautiful the exterior chassis is. Most gaming laptops around this price are eyesores. The main downside to the Alienware 15 is the screen, which has some noticeably bad color reproduction. The visuals have a desaturated look that annoys me, which is common on these budget gaming laptops.
The Lenovo LOQ 15 with the RTX 5060 has been my top pick for affordable gaming laptops throughout most of the year, as it has been the cheapest way to get decent gaming performance without any major compromises to the laptop. It has a much better display than the Alienware 15, for example. However, it's recently gone up by hundreds of dollars in price, which is frustrating. Its high-quality display still makes it stand out, though, and it's worth the couple hundred extra dollars in my book.
There’s a whole world of gaming laptops outside the budget tier, though. I’ve tested an assortment of options, and I always come back to the Razer Blade 14 and Razer Blade 16. Portable, minimalist, and extremely well-made, they have rightfully earned their reputation as the MacBooks of PC gaming—along with the MacBook Pro–like price tag. Their sleek design means they work just as well for school or work as they do for gaming, without the bulk of a traditional gaming laptop. While there are more powerful options out there, nothing quite matches the Razer Blade.
Other Good Laptops I’ve Tested
If you choose one of the laptops above, you will be very happy with your purchase. However, if you are looking for a specific feature or a different price point, I have included a few other options below. While each of these recently tested laptops has at least one minor drawback, they could still be the perfect choice depending on your needs and currently available discounts.
Microsoft Surface Laptop 13.8 for $988: The Surface Laptop 13.8 (also known as the 7th Edition) was one of my favorite laptops throughout the 2024 and 2025, primarily because of its premium build quality, great battery life, and 3:2 aspect ratio screen. And while I still love this laptop, it’s risen in price dramatically and no longer feels like as good of a value, especially since it’s two years old at this point. The 2024 model now starts at $1,200, though I've occasionally seen it dip under $1,000. The next-generation model with the Snapdragon X2 chips costs $1,700. I'm seeing that price now come down to $1,350 on discount.
Dell 14 Plus for $1,000: There was a time in 2025 when the Dell 14 Plus was as affordable as $600. It was easily the best deal in the world of Windows laptops, primarily because the Dell 14 Plus has a 2560 x 1600 display and a smooth touchpad, two things laptops at that price typically lack. These days, it's up to $1,000, though for a 1 TB configuration, that is still a fabulous price. The XPS 13 is the better overall laptop, but the Dell 14 Plus has more ports and comes with more storage for the money.
Dell 14S for $1,270: This is the 2026 successor to the Dell 14 Plus, which I recommended above. This is a solid laptop, sporting a premium design and a very reflective OLED display. It performs well too, thanks to the latest Intel Core Ultra Series 3 chip. The Dell 14 Plus is a better deal right now, though, so I would point you to the Dell 14 Plus or Dell XPS 13 instead.
Framework Laptop 13 for $849: This unique laptop is fully repairable and the internals are accessible, including the CPU and motherboard. There’s nothing else like it out there. The Framework Laptop 16 gets you better performance, while the Framework Laptop 12 is the budget option. Then, there’s the Framework Laptop 13 Pro, which comes with some more premium features like a touchscreen and a haptic feedback touchpad.
Asus Zenbook A16 for $2,200: This second edition of the Zenbook A16 is still incredibly light, and now it comes with the second-generation Snapdragon X2 chips. It’s unique for its portability, and the Qualcomm chips deliver great battery life and performance. However, given the dramatic price increase, I’d suggest buying the 2025 model instead, which is under $1,000.
Asus CX14 Chromebook for $189: A Chromebook under $300 is never going to be compromise-free, as is true with the CX14. Keep your expectations in check (especially regarding the screen and the touchpad), but for a laptop that frequently sells under $200, this will serve you well enough.
Alienware 16X Aurora for $2,480: Another solid gaming laptop, this one comes with the typical Alienware flair. Its standout features are its higher-resolution display and great build quality.
